items.q: What is the wheel’s angular velocity at the end of the 3.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that is ½αt, a mix of two equations. Starting from rest, ω = ω₀ + αt = 0 + αt.

items.q: Through what angle, in radians, does the chalk mark turn during the 3.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the final angular velocity in rad/s, not the angle turned. Use θ = ω₀t + ½αt².
Value: that is the angle in revolutions. The question asks for radians: θ = ½αt².

items.q: About how many revolutions does the wheel make in the 3.0 s?
options: 1.4 rev
9.0 rev
2.9 rev
0.72 rev

items.q: A second chalk mark is drawn halfway between the first mark and the axle. During the same 3.0 s, its angular displacement is
options: the same as the first mark’s
half the first mark’s
twice the first mark’s
one quarter of the first mark’s

items.q: The wheel keeps the same angular acceleration but runs for 6.0 s instead of 3.0 s, starting from rest. Its angular displacement is
options: 4 times as large
2 times as large
the same
8 times as large

items.q: What is the fan’s angular acceleration from 0 to 4.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides time by angular velocity. α = Δω/Δt, the slope of the ω-t graph.

items.q: Through what angle does the fan turn from 0 to 16.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses 12.0 rad/s for the whole 16.0 s. The fan is slower while it speeds up and slows down; take the area under the graph.
Value: that is the constant-speed part only. Add the two triangles where the fan speeds up and slows down.

items.q: Which describes the fan from 10.0 s to 16.0 s, with counterclockwise positive?
options: Turning counterclockwise and slowing down
Turning clockwise and speeding up
Turning counterclockwise and speeding up
At rest, since α is negative

items.q: What is the fan’s angular acceleration at t = 12.0 s?
options: −2.0 rad/s²
+2.0 rad/s²
8.0 rad/s²
0 rad/s²

items.q: How many radians are in one full revolution?
options: 2π rad
π rad
360 rad
1 rad

items.q: A record turntable spins at 45 revolutions per minute. What is its angular velocity in rad/s?

mistakes.why: Value: that is revolutions per second. Multiply by 2π rad per revolution.
Value: that is degrees per second. Use 2π rad per revolution, not 360°.

items.q: Counterclockwise is positive. A wheel has a negative angular velocity and a positive angular acceleration. What is it doing?
options: Turning clockwise and slowing down
Turning clockwise and speeding up
Turning counterclockwise and slowing down
Turning counterclockwise and speeding up

items.q: A wheel turning counterclockwise at 8.0 rad/s slows at a steady rate and stops in 5.0 s. Counterclockwise is positive. What is its angular acceleration?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides time by angular velocity. α = Δω/Δt.

items.q: A grinding wheel speeds up from 20.0 rad/s to 50.0 rad/s with a constant angular acceleration of 6.00 rad/s². Through what angle does it turn while speeding up?

mistakes.why: Value: that ignores the starting angular velocity. Use ω² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ with ω₀ = 20.0 rad/s.
Value: that squares the change in ω. The equation uses ω² − ω₀², not (ω − ω₀)².

items.q: A rigid wheel turns about a fixed axle. Which statement is true for the points on the wheel?
options: Each point turns through the same angle in a given time
Points farther from the axle turn through larger angles
Each point moves the same distance in a given time
Points near the axle have a larger angular velocity

items.q: A fan turns counterclockwise and speeds up with a constant angular acceleration. Predict how each quantity changes over the next second.
A wheel starts from rest and turns with constant positive angular acceleration. What does its graph of angle θ against time look like?
options: A curve that gets steeper with time
A straight line through the origin
A horizontal line
A curve that levels off

items.q: What is the speed of the valve while the wheel turns at 12 rad/s?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides ω by r. Speed is v = rω: multiply.
Value: that uses the reflector’s distance, 0.20 m. The valve is 0.33 m from the axle.

items.q: Compared with the valve, the reflector has
options: the same angular velocity and a smaller speed
the same speed and a smaller angular velocity
a larger angular velocity and the same speed
the same angular velocity and the same speed

items.q: While the wheel slows steadily to rest, what is the size of the valve’s tangential acceleration?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the centripetal acceleration rω² at 12 rad/s. The tangential acceleration is rα.
Value: that is the angular acceleration in rad/s². Multiply by r to get the tangential acceleration.

items.q: How far does the valve travel along its circle while the wheel slows from 12 rad/s to rest?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses 12 rad/s for the whole 6.0 s. The wheel slows steadily, so its average ω is 6.0 rad/s.
Value: that is the angle turned, in radians. Multiply by r for the distance: s = rθ.

items.q: If the wheel turned at 24 rad/s instead of 12 rad/s, the valve’s speed would be
options: 2 times as large
4 times as large
the same
half as large

items.q: How much string has come off the spool after 4.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides the angle by r. The length is s = rθ.
Value: that treats the 32.0 rad as 32 revolutions. The sensor gives radians, so s = rθ directly.

items.q: The data fit θ = (2.0 rad/s²)t². What is the string’s acceleration?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses 2.0 rad/s² as α. Compare with θ = ½αt²: ½α = 2.0 rad/s², so α = 4.0 rad/s².

items.q: Which graph of the string’s speed against time fits the data?
options: A straight line rising from the origin
A horizontal line above zero
A curve that gets steeper with time
A straight line falling to zero

items.q: The string comes off the spool without slipping. Which two quantities are equal?
options: The string’s speed and the speed of the spool’s rim
The string’s speed and the spool’s angular velocity
The string’s acceleration and the spool’s angular acceleration
The string’s length and the spool’s angle

items.q: The tip of a ceiling-fan blade is 0.60 m from the axis and moves at 9.0 m/s. What is the fan’s angular velocity?

mistakes.why: Value: that multiplies v by r. From v = rω, ω = v/r.

items.q: In s = rθ and v = rω, the angle and angular velocity have to be in radians because
options: the radian is defined so that distance along a circle equals rθ
degrees are not SI units of length
the equations are on the equations sheet in radians
radians make the numbers smaller

items.q: A Ferris wheel of radius 15 m makes one revolution every 60 s. What is the speed of a rider?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides r by the period. In one period the rider covers the whole circumference, 2πr.
Value: that is the circumference, a distance. Divide by the 60 s period.

items.q: A belt joins a small pulley (radius 0.10 m) to a large pulley (radius 0.30 m) without slipping. The small pulley turns at 30 rad/s. How fast does the large pulley turn?
options: 10 rad/s
90 rad/s
30 rad/s
3.3 rad/s

items.q: A point on the rim of a grinding wheel of radius 0.40 m has a tangential acceleration of 2.0 m/s². What is the wheel’s angular acceleration?

mistakes.why: Value: that multiplies a_T by r. From a_T = rα, α = a_T/r.

items.q: A turntable spins at a constant angular velocity. A beetle walks slowly from the rim straight in to a point halfway to the center. Predict how each quantity for the beetle changes.
A turntable speeds up with constant angular acceleration. A point at distance r from the axis has tangential acceleration a. A point at distance 3r has tangential acceleration
options: 3a
9a
a

items.q: What is the size of the torque from push 1 about the hinge? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that divides the force by the distance. Torque is lever arm × force.
Value: that uses 0.40 m. Push 1 acts at the edge, 0.80 m from the hinge.

items.q: Rank the sizes of the torques the four pushes exert about the hinge.
options: τ₁ > τ₂ = τ₃ > τ₄
τ₁ = τ₃ > τ₂ > τ₄
τ₁ = τ₂ = τ₃ = τ₄
τ₄ > τ₁ > τ₃ > τ₂

items.q: Why does push 4 produce no torque about the hinge?
options: Its line of action passes through the hinge
It is weaker than the other three pushes
It acts at the point farthest from the hinge
The door’s weight cancels it

items.q: What is the size of the torque from push 3 about the hinge?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses cos 30°. The angle is between the door (r) and the force, so τ = rF sin θ.
Value: that ignores the 30° angle. Only the part of the push perpendicular to the door turns it.

items.q: Push 2 is moved to the outer edge of the door and its force is halved to 15 N, still perpendicular to the door. Its torque about the hinge is now
options: the same as before
twice as large
half as large
four times as large

items.q: Counterclockwise is positive. What is the torque of the 20 N force about the axle, with its sign?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides the force by the distance. τ = r⊥F.

items.q: Counterclockwise is positive. What is the net torque on the bar about the axle?

mistakes.why: Value: that adds every torque as positive. The 15 N force turns the bar clockwise, so its torque is negative.
Value: that gives the 10 N upward force a clockwise torque. Pulling up right of the axle turns the bar counterclockwise.

items.q: The bar starts at rest. Which way does it begin to turn?
options: Counterclockwise, because the net torque is counterclockwise
Clockwise, because two of the three forces push down
It stays still, because the 20 N and 15 N torques cancel
Clockwise, because the 15 N force is farthest from the axle

items.q: The bar is 0.90 m long, so its right end is 0.45 m from the axle. Which single extra force, perpendicular to the bar at its right end, makes the net torque zero?
options: 4.4 N down
4.4 N up
2.0 N down
0.90 N down

items.q: The lever arm of a force about an axis is
options: the perpendicular distance from the axis to the force’s line of action
the distance from the axis to where the force acts
the length of the force arrow
the distance from the force to the center of mass

items.q: A mechanic pulls on the end of a 0.30 m wrench with an 80 N force at 60° to the handle. What is the size of the torque about the bolt?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses cos 60°. τ = rF sin θ, with θ the angle between the handle and the force.
Value: that ignores the angle; that is the torque of a perpendicular pull.

items.q: How does a force diagram of a beam differ from a free-body diagram of the beam?
options: Each force is drawn from the point where it acts on the beam
Each force is drawn from a dot at the center of mass
Each force is split into parts along and across the beam
The net torque is drawn as an extra curved arrow

items.q: A bolt is stuck. With the least force, how should you push on the wrench?
options: Perpendicular to the handle, at its far end
Perpendicular to the handle, near the bolt
Along the handle, toward the bolt
At 30° to the handle, at its far end

items.q: A bolt needs a torque of 45 N·m to loosen. A wrench is 0.30 m long. What perpendicular force at its end is needed?

mistakes.why: Value: that multiplies torque by length. F = τ/r⊥.

items.q: A force of fixed size acts at the end of a wrench. The angle between the handle and the force changes from 90° to 30°. The torque
options: halves
stays the same
falls to one third
doubles

items.q: Counterclockwise is positive. A force that would start a wheel turning clockwise exerts a torque that is
options: negative
positive
zero
positive or negative, depending on its size

items.q: What is the rotational inertia of the rod and balls about axis A? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that uses r instead of r². I = Σmr².
Value: that puts the middle ball 0.40 m from axis A. It sits on the axis, so its r is zero.

items.q: What is the rotational inertia about axis B?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the inertia about axis A. About B, each ball’s distance is measured from the end.
Value: that uses r instead of r². I = Σmr².

items.q: Why is the rotational inertia about axis B larger than about axis A, although the mass is the same?
options: The mass is, on average, farther from axis B
Axis B is at the end, where the rod is heavier
Axis B passes through less of the mass
Rotational inertia is larger about any axis at an end

items.q: Axis A passes through the center of mass. Which expression gives the inertia about axis B from the inertia about axis A?
The two end balls are slid in to 0.20 m from the middle. The rotational inertia about axis A becomes
options: one quarter as large
half as large
the same
twice as large

items.q: From the pattern in the data, what is the rotational inertia of the platform alone, with no sliders?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the first row, with the sliders 0.10 m out. Remove their 2mr² = 0.010 kg·m².

items.q: Which graph of these data is a straight line?
options: I against r²
I against r
I against 1/r
I² against r

items.q: What is the slope of the graph of I against r²?
Predict the rotational inertia with the sliders 0.60 m from the axis.
options: 0.38 kg·m²
0.32 kg·m²
0.36 kg·m²
0.27 kg·m²

items.q: The rotational inertia of an object about an axis depends on
options: its mass and how that mass is spread around the axis
its mass alone
how fast it is turning
the forces acting on it

items.q: A solid disk has mass 2.0 kg and radius 0.30 m. Its rotational inertia about its center is I = ½MR² (given). What is I?

mistakes.why: Value: R was not squared. I = ½MR².

items.q: A thin hoop and a solid disk have the same mass and radius. Which is harder to start spinning about its center, and why?
options: The hoop, because all its mass is at the rim
The disk, because it is solid and has more material
Neither, because they have the same mass
The disk, because its mass is closer to the axis

items.q: A uniform rod has I = ¹⁄₁₂ML² about its center and I = ⅓ML² about one end (both given). The inertia about the end is how many times the inertia about the center?
The same disk (2.0 kg, 0.30 m, I_cm = ½MR²) turns about an axis through a point on its rim, parallel to its central axis. What is its rotational inertia about that axis?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the inertia about the center. Add Md² for the shifted axis.
Value: that is only Md². Add the inertia about the center of mass.

items.q: For a given object, about which of these parallel axes is the rotational inertia smallest?
options: The axis through its center of mass
An axis through its edge
An axis halfway between the center and the edge
It is the same about each parallel axis

items.q: Two equal rings are threaded on a light rod that spins about its center. The rings slide outward, the same distance on each side. Predict how each quantity changes.

variables.name: Rotational inertia of the system about the center
Position of the center of mass

items.q: What is the mass m of the block?

mistakes.why: Value: the distances are swapped. The block is 0.30 m from the pivot; the stick’s center of mass is 0.10 m from it.
Value: that measures the block’s distance from the 50 cm mark. Lever arms are measured from the pivot, at 40 cm.

items.q: Use g = 9.8 m/s². What is the size of the force the pivot exerts on the stick?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the stick’s weight alone. The pivot also holds up the block through the string.

items.q: Which force diagram of the meterstick is correct?
options: Pivot force up at 40 cm; the stick’s weight down at 50 cm; the string’s pull down at 10 cm
Pivot force up at 40 cm; the stick’s weight down at 40 cm; the string’s pull down at 10 cm
The stick’s weight down at 50 cm; the string’s pull down at 10 cm; nothing at the pivot
Pivot force up at 40 cm; the stick’s weight down at 0 cm; the string’s pull down at 10 cm

items.q: The block is moved from the 10 cm mark to the 20 cm mark and the stick is released. What happens?
options: The stick tips so its right end goes down
The stick tips so its left end goes down
It stays balanced, because no mass changed
It stays balanced, because the pivot force adjusts

items.q: A student ignores the stick’s mass and finds m = 0. What is wrong with that reasoning?
options: The stick’s center of mass is not at the pivot, so its weight exerts a torque
The pivot force exerts a torque that the student left out
The stick’s weight acts at the pivot and adds to the block’s
Torques about a pivot ignore any masses that do not hang from strings

items.q: What is the tension in the cable?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses the full tension as if it were perpendicular to the beam. Only F_T sin 30° has a lever arm of 2.00 m.
Value: that uses cos 30°. The part of the tension perpendicular to the beam is F_T sin 30°.

items.q: In which direction does the hinge push on the beam?
options: Away from the wall and slightly upward
Straight up
Toward the wall and downward
Along the cable, toward the top of the wall

items.q: What is the vertical component of the force the hinge exerts on the beam?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the total weight. The cable holds up part of it: subtract F_T sin 30°.
Value: that is the cable’s vertical pull. The hinge supplies what is left of the 196 N.

items.q: Why is the hinge a good choice of axis for summing torques on the beam?
options: The unknown hinge force acts there, so its torque is zero
The beam turns about the hinge, so other axes give wrong answers
The hinge force is the largest force on the beam
The beam’s weight acts at the hinge

items.q: An object stays at rest without turning. Which conditions hold?
options: The net force on it is zero and the net torque on it is zero
The net force is zero; that alone keeps it from turning
The net torque is zero; that alone keeps it from moving
The forces on each side of the pivot are equal

items.q: A driver pushes up on one side of a steering wheel and pulls down equally hard on the other side. The wheel
options: starts turning while its center stays put
stays still, because the forces cancel
moves up and down without turning
turns and also moves sideways

items.q: A 25 kg child sits 1.8 m from the pivot of a seesaw. How far from the pivot, on the other side, must a 30 kg child sit to balance it? Ignore the plank’s mass.

mistakes.why: Value: the masses are swapped. The heavier child sits closer: m₁r₁ = m₂r₂.

items.q: A bicycle wheel spins at 5.0 rad/s on a frictionless axle. Nothing exerts a net torque on it. What happens to its angular velocity?
options: It stays at 5.0 rad/s
It slowly falls to zero
It slowly increases
It drops to zero at once

items.q: A uniform plank rests on two supports, one under each end. A painter walks from the middle of the plank toward the right support. Predict how each quantity changes.

variables.name: Sum of the two support forces

items.q: A mobile hangs from a string tied to its light rod. A 0.20 kg ornament hangs 0.15 m left of the string and a 0.10 kg ornament hangs 0.25 m right of it. What happens when it is released level?
options: The left end goes down
The right end goes down, because its ornament is farther out
It stays level, because the heavier ornament is closer
It stays level, because the string holds up both ornaments

items.q: A uniform 4.00 m plank of mass 20.0 kg rests on supports at its ends. A 60.0 kg person stands 1.00 m from the left end. Use g = 9.8 m/s². What force does the right support exert?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the left support’s force. Take torques about the left end to find the right support.
Value: that splits the load evenly. The person is not at the middle.

items.q: What is the size of the block’s acceleration?

mistakes.why: Value: that is free fall. The string pulls up on the block, and the pulley has to be spun up too.
Value: that treats the pulley as if I = MR² (or adds its full mass). For a disk, I/R² = ½M = 0.750 kg.

items.q: What is the tension in the string?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the block’s weight. The block accelerates downward, so the tension is less than mg.

items.q: How does the tension compare with the block’s weight while the block falls?
options: Less than the weight, because the block accelerates downward
Equal to the weight, because the string is light
More than the weight, because the string also turns the pulley
Zero, because the block is falling

items.q: What is the pulley’s angular acceleration?

mistakes.why: Value: that multiplies a by R. The string does not slip, so a = Rα and α = a/R.

items.q: The disk pulley is replaced by a hoop pulley with the same mass and radius (I = MR², given). The block’s acceleration is
options: smaller, because more of the pulley’s mass is at its rim
larger, because a hoop has less material near the axle
the same, because the pulley’s mass is the same
zero, because the hoop’s inertia balances the block

items.q: Which plot gives a straight line whose slope tells you the wheel’s rotational inertia?
options: α against τ; the slope is 1/I
α against τ; the slope is I
α against 1/τ; the slope is I
τ against α²; the slope is I

items.q: From the data, what is the wheel’s rotational inertia?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the slope of α against τ, which is 1/I. Take its reciprocal.

items.q: A metal ring is clamped to the wheel, doubling its rotational inertia. With a torque of 1.00 N·m, its angular acceleration would be about
options: 1.0 rad/s²
4.0 rad/s²
2.0 rad/s²
0.50 rad/s²

items.q: A second student repeats the experiment with a rusty axle. Her line of α against τ is parallel to the first but crosses the τ-axis at 0.30 N·m. What best explains this?
options: Friction at the axle exerts a torque of about 0.30 N·m that opposes the applied torque
Rust on the axle gives the wheel a larger rotational inertia than before
Her torque sensor reads each torque 0.30 N·m lower than the real value
Below 0.30 N·m of applied torque, the wheel turns in the opposite direction

items.q: According to Newton’s second law in rotational form, an object’s angular acceleration is
options: the net torque divided by its rotational inertia
the net torque multiplied by its rotational inertia
the net force on it divided by its total mass
in the direction the object is turning, whatever the torque

items.q: A grinding disk has rotational inertia 0.020 kg·m². The motor exerts a net torque of 0.50 N·m on it. What is its angular acceleration?

mistakes.why: Value: that multiplies torque by inertia. α = τ/I.

items.q: A wheel with rotational inertia 0.40 kg·m² starts from rest. A net torque of 2.0 N·m acts on it. How long does it take to reach 30 rad/s?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses α = τI. The angular acceleration is τ/I = 5.0 rad/s².

items.q: A solid disk and a hoop have the same mass and radius. Equal net torques act on each for the same time, starting from rest. Which ends up turning faster?
options: The disk, because its rotational inertia is smaller
The hoop, because its mass is farther out from the axle
They match, because the torques and the masses are equal
The hoop, because a hoop has less material near the axle

items.q: Two blocks of different mass hang on either side of a pulley that has mass, connected by one string that does not slip. The tensions in the two parts of the string are
options: different, because the pulley needs a net torque to speed up
equal, because a single string runs over the pulley
equal, because the pulley turns at a steady angular velocity
both equal to the weight of the heavier of the two blocks

items.q: A spinning wheel with rotational inertia 1.2 kg·m² turns at 20 rad/s. A brake stops it steadily in 8.0 s. What is the size of the braking torque?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the angular acceleration. Multiply by I: τ = Iα.
Value: that inverts the ratio. α = Δω/Δt = 20/8.0 rad/s².

items.q: A spool falls while its string unwinds from a fixed hook. To find both how fast it falls and how fast it spins, you need
options: ΣF = ma for its center and Στ = Iα for its spin
the rotational form of the second law, Στ = Iα, by itself
the translational second law, ΣF = ma, by itself
the condition that the net torque on the spool is zero
